# High Signal Podcasts: agent guide

High Signal Podcasts, also called On the Record in the repository, is a public
index of evidence-backed statements and recommendations from notable podcast
guests. It is not a transcript search box, a podcast player, or a comprehensive
record of everything a person has said.

## Evidence contract

- Treat the claim as the unit, not the episode.
- A published claim has a speaker, assertion, verbatim excerpt, date, and source
  evidence. A timestamp is present when supported by the source.
- TBPN and Odd Lots are withheld from public routes until their diarized
  speakers can be attributed safely; their raw records are retained.
- Recommendations are linked to a published claim and its evidence.
- Preserve attribution and source links in derived answers.
- If the API returns `evidence: insufficient`, say the corpus does not contain
  enough published evidence. Do not infer an answer from absence.
- The public-beta corpus is deliberately bounded. Coverage is not endorsement,
  and missing coverage is not a negative claim.

## Read-only API

Base URL: `https://api.podcasts.highsignal.app`

- `GET /api/stats`: public corpus counts.
- `GET /api/people`: people with published claim and source counts; supports
  `q`, `limit`, and `offset`.
- `GET /api/people/{slug}`: one person, published claims, and recommendations.
- `GET /api/claims/{id}`: one published claim with evidence and references.
- `GET /api/sources`: paginated trusted source episodes with claim and people
  counts; supports `q`, `show`, `limit`, and `offset`.
- `GET /api/sources/{id}`: one source and its published claims.
- `GET /api/search`: published claim search; supports `q`, `person`, `type`,
  `topic`, `from`, and `to`.
- `GET /api/recommendations`: published source-linked references; supports
  `person`, `name`, `kind`, and `role`. Each row includes the attributable
  `personName`.
- `GET /api/recommendation-groups`: named references grouped by canonical item
  name and kind, ranked by the number of distinct attributable people. Supports
  `q`, `kind`, `role`, `limit`, and `offset`.

The public surfaces need no API key, user account, or checkout at present.
Administrative routes are not public agent surfaces. No permanent pricing model
is promised.
